input.brief: MSP website for managed IT services in Texas

direction.name: The well-kept board
direction.idea: The whole page is a board of tiles fitted edge to edge with narrow gaps, like a tidy desk seen from above. Each tile is one thing: the name, a statement, a photograph, a number, a link, a short list. There is no hero and no sequence of bands; the page is one continuous composition that the eye roams. It suits subjects with many small true things to show (a studio with work, writing, clients and news; a product with several distinct capabilities) and it replaces the generic bento by having real content in every tile and a strict system for sizes.
direction.composition: A 12-column grid with 8px gaps and 8–12px outer margins, filled completely, no empty cells. Tiles use only four sizes (for example 6×4, 6×2, 3×2, 3×4 in column × row units of about 90px). Every tile is a flat filled rectangle: ground colour one step from the page, or a palette colour, or a photograph covering it. One radius everywhere (0, or 6–10px). The first screen contains: a name tile (the name at display size, the largest type on the page) with the wordmark set large, a statement tile with the description at 28–40px, two or three image tiles and one action tile in the accent colour. Text inside tiles is top-left aligned with 20–24px padding and never centred. Below the first screen the board continues with the same sizes; the last row is the footer made of tiles.
direction.typography: One grotesk in two weights. Inside tiles: a large size for single statements, a small size for lists. No uppercase labels in tile corners.
direction.colour: Page ground, tile ground one step lighter or darker, and one or two palette colours on selected tiles. Photographs supply the rest.
direction.imagery: Photographs fill whole tiles with `object-fit: cover`; choose images that crop well to both wide and tall tiles.
direction.richness: The fit. A full board with consistent gaps and varied tile contents is satisfying in the way a packed suitcase is.
direction.pitfalls: Tiles are filled, never outlined, and never carry shadows. Do not put an icon and a two-line feature blurb in every tile; vary what tiles hold. Decide the phone layout as its own board: two columns, tiles re-ordered so the name and statement lead.

hero.name: Sheet with a text cell
hero.blueprint: The whole viewport is a sheet of photographs: six columns with 12px gaps and 12px outer margins, each column a vertical stack of frames at natural ratios with square corners. Each column starts at a different vertical offset (0, -90, -40, -130, -20, -70px) so rows never line up and the top and bottom frames are cropped by the viewport. Every frame has a flat strip 28px tall fused to its bottom edge in a solid palette colour, carrying one line of 13px text (a title or a place); strip colours rotate through four values. There is no header. In columns 3-4, starting at 28% of the height, one cell of the sheet is not a photograph but a filled panel in the tone opposite to the ground, 410px tall, sitting on the grid like any other frame with the same gaps on all sides. Inside it, top-left aligned on 24px padding: the wordmark at 28px, one sentence at 20px on up to three lines, the single action as a filled rectangle, and three text links on one line at the panel's foot.
hero.mobile: The text panel spans the full width as the first block, about 40% of the screen height, with the wordmark at 7vw, the sentence at 17px and the action full width. Under it the sheet resumes in two columns with 8px gaps, the right column started 60px higher than the left, colour strips kept on every frame. The links sit in one row at the panel's foot.
hero.headline: The wordmark at 28px plus one sentence of up to 70 characters inside the panel; nothing is set at display size.

type.note: A geometric grotesque with Scandinavian restraint: round letters, even colour, nothing decorative. Suits logistics, health, property and corporate sites that need to look clear and dependable.

palette.name: Night and cornflower
palette.note: Blue-black ground and slate panels with silver-white text fill the page; no section changes colour. Cornflower blue marks the buttons and at most one word in a heading.

motion.name: Shutter image
motion.description: The one hero or showcase image opens from an edge with a clip-path over about 1.1 seconds while the picture inside settles from 1.12 scale to rest. Use it once, on the image that matters most; later images simply are there. Recipe: 'Image shutter' in references/motion.md.

sections.name: Statement tiles
sections.blueprint: A board of filled tiles with 8px gaps and 8px outer margins: 12 columns by two rows of 38svh each. Tile A, columns 1–8 across both rows, is the darkest tile and carries a slogan of two to four words in capitals at clamp(64px, 9vw, 132px), leading 0.86, on two lines, set hard against the tile's 20px left padding and bottom-aligned. Tile B, columns 9–12 of row one, is a pale tile with one word or figure at the same size, bottom-aligned, cropped by `overflow: hidden` if it runs long. Tile C, columns 9–12 of row two, is a photograph covering the tile. Below the board a fourth tile spans all 12 columns in the page ground colour: its left half is empty and a text of 90–130 words at 22–24px with leading 1.35 runs in columns 7–12 with 40px padding. No separate heading: the slogan in tile A is the heading.
sections.mobile: A two-column board with 6px gaps. The slogan tile spans both columns at 46svh with type at 17vw on two lines; the word tile and the photograph tile sit side by side as squares; the long text tile spans both columns with 20px padding at 18px.

sections.name: Statement cell, dark rows
sections.blueprint: Two halves butted together, each 50vw wide and at least 90svh tall, with no gap. Left half, in a pale tone: the heading in three short lines at clamp(36px, 4.2vw, 68px), its middle line pushed flush right while the first and third stay flush left (text-align set per line), so the block zigzags inside the cell. A two-sentence paragraph of 30ch sits at the bottom-left and the single action at the bottom-right on the same baseline. Right half, in the darkest tone: four or five rows of equal height filling it, told apart by alternating two near-black tones, not by lines. Each row is a three-part grid: a title at 28px (5 parts), a short paragraph at 16px (4 parts) and a plain list of three terms at 15px (3 parts), all top-aligned with 28px padding. No images anywhere in the section.
sections.mobile: The halves stack. The light cell comes first at 70svh with the zigzag heading at 10vw and the paragraph at its foot. The dark rows follow at full width; each row stacks its title and paragraph, and its three terms run inline as one sentence separated by commas. Rows keep the alternating tones.

sections.name: One image across tiles
sections.blueprint: One photograph is cut across a board of tiles. A grid of six columns and four rows with 8px gaps spans the full width between 12px margins; every tile is square (aspect-ratio: 1). Each tile shows its own piece of the same image: set the photograph as every tile's background at background-size: 600% 400% and step background-position by column and row, so the picture reads whole through the gaps. Five of the twenty-four tiles are swapped for flat colour tiles from the palette, never two adjacent: one holds the heading (two to four words at 2.6vw, top-left, 16px padding), three hold one fact each at 18px, one holds the action. On hover a tile's piece scales to 108% inside its own clip. Choose a photograph with one clear subject, so the board is legible at a glance.
sections.mobile: Three columns by six rows with 6px gaps, the photograph re-cut at background-size 300% 600% from a portrait crop. Four colour tiles only; the heading tile spans two columns in the top row with the heading at 6vw. Facts drop to 15px.

sections.name: The action tile
sections.blueprint: The close is one row of the board. Three filled tiles sit side by side with 8–14px gaps, all 360px tall and sharing one radius: a wide centre tile spanning columns 3–10 in the accent colour, flanked by two narrow tiles (columns 1–2 and 11–12) that run off the left and right viewport edges, as if the row had been cropped from a longer one. The centre tile holds, left-aligned and vertically centred with 40px padding: a heading of three to five words at 40px, two lines at 17px, and the action. The action is either one rectangular button or an email field 420px wide in the paper colour with the submit button nested inside its right end. The flanking tiles hold no text: one is a photograph covering the tile, the other a flat palette colour. No shadows, no outlines.
sections.mobile: The accent tile runs full width, about 300px tall, heading at 28px, field and button stacked at full width. The two flanking tiles follow beneath as a pair, each half width and 120px tall, with the same gap and the same radius.

sections.name: The mark, built large
sections.blueprint: On a flat colour field, the brand closes the page as a construction rather than as set type. Across the full content width and about 34svh tall, the wordmark is built from blocks: each letter is knocked out of its own solid rectangle in a palette colour, the rectangles differ in height (60–100% of the band) and butt together with 4px gaps, bottoms on one line. Where the project has a simple geometric mark or motif, enlarge that instead, drawn as inline SVG from flat rectangles, circles and quarter-arcs with the same 4px gaps. Below, 56px lower: four columns of plain links at 15px across columns 1–8, and two addresses or contact lines in columns 9–12. A last row carries the copyright at the left and one small filled button at the right. Space and the block construction do all the separating.
sections.mobile: The block wordmark spans the full width at about 22svh tall; a long name breaks into two rows of blocks. Link columns go two across at 15px, contact lines beneath at full width, then copyright and the small button on one row.

references.name: Aspen Search
references.idea: The page is a ruled tile system with no margins: the two-word name is split across cells that alternate type, dithered canvas, black and one mint green.
references.hero: A 60px top bar ruled into cells: black logo square, local time, nav links starting at the centre line, a theme toggle and a black contact cell flush right. Below, the viewport is a two-by-two grid divided by 1px black lines, no outer margin. Top-left is white with the first word of the name at 12.5vw, weight 450, sitting bottom-left. Top-right and bottom-left cells hold a black-and-white dithered canvas crossed by large pale-grey blade shapes that ignore cell borders. The bottom-right quadrant splits into a black cell (24px white summary, mono caps action row at its base) and a mint cell (second statement, client-logo marquee along the bottom).
references.type: Suisse Intl at weight 450 for everything, tracking about -0.02em; Suisse Intl Mono in small caps for actions, bullet lists and footer. Wordmark 180px against 24px statements and 16px body. Later headings switch to all caps at about 9vw with leading near 0.9.
references.colour: #ffffff #232323 #d9d9d9 #a1ffcb #969797 — White, near-black and two greys fill the cells; a single mint green floods whole tiles (a statement, a stat, the closing call to action) as the only colour. Cool and flat.
references.imagery: A canvas of 1-bit ordered-dither dots with soft tonal blobs, overlaid with flat pale-grey shards taken from the logo; services get white wireframe line drawings of spheres. No photography anywhere.
references.layout: Zero page margin: everything is edge-to-edge cells on a two-column grid with halves subdivided, separated by 1px rules. Sections differ only by cell fill and cell height. Type always sits top-left or bottom-left in its cell with about 20px padding; some cells are left deliberately empty.

sections.description: The second screen continues the hero grid: a black cell carries a two-line all-caps slogan at about 9vw set hard against its left edge; a light grey cell top-right holds the second word of the name at the same giant size as the first, bottom-aligned; dither canvas fills the rest. Then a white row where the left half is empty and a 24px long-form text runs only in the right column.

Stair-stepped tiles instead of a row. A tall mint cell fills the left half with one figure at about 5vw in its top-left corner and nothing else. On the right, a shorter black tile starts higher with a white figure top-left and a small caption at its bottom edge; a grey tile sits to its right, stepped down, same internal layout. The tiles' unequal heights leave white notches.

Left half: a light grey cell with a three-line all-caps heading whose middle line is pushed to the right edge, a small paragraph low in the cell and a black mono-caps button bottom-right. Right half: black, split by hairlines into stacked rows; each row has a tiny mono index, a 28px title, a short paragraph in a second column, a white wireframe drawing and a mono caps list with small mint square bullets.

A grid of cells: white cell with a short statement top-left; a cell with a plain nav list; a cell with two small analogue clock icons and city times; a hairline row with email left and a social link right. Below, a black cell with the logo and lowercase wordmark centred large, beside a mint cell with a heading top-left and a thin diagonal arrow drawn into its bottom-right corner.

steal: Rule the whole viewport into cells with 1px lines and no page margin, then give the nav, the headline, the summary and the proof each its own cell with a flat fill.
Split a two-word brand name across two cells on consecutive screens at the same giant size, so scrolling completes the name.
Use a 1-bit ordered-dither texture as the picture in otherwise empty cells and let large flat logo fragments cross the cell borders to tie the grid together.
references.media: One halftone canvas of the brand mark is seen only through chosen cells of the tile grid, about half the hero area, and returns in sticky half panels and as a full-bleed canvas behind knockout words. Portraits are high-key black and white in a staggered row with offset heights, client logos keep their brand colours inside their own tiles, and there is no video and no rounded corner anywhere.
references.motion: A dark screen gives way at about 1.2s to a small mark on a 20s coin spin, the white grid arrives by 2.5s with the name rising through a mask, and the dither resolves by 4.5s. Lenis drives CSS sticky stacking (12 sticky elements, no pins): hero rows slide over each other and stat tiles lock under the header one by one; text fades in by line over 1000ms cubic-bezier(0.23,1,0.32,1) in 100ms steps (193 WAAPI calls), and a theme toggle wipes the page with a 1.2s clip-path sweep.

references.name: Oimachi
references.idea: A studio homepage that behaves like a dense dashboard: work, posts, experiments and testimonials tiled edge to edge with 8px gutters instead of spaced-out sections.
references.archetype: other: left statement over media row with posts sidebar
references.hero: Charcoal ground (#181818) with only 8px side margins. Top-left: a round logo, then five tiny black rectangular chips with bold white 13px labels; top-right a contact chip and a theme toggle. The headline starts at the left margin about 160px down: two lines of light grotesk at 52px (3.6vw), tight tracking, with one word in italic serif. From 280px to the bottom edge runs a three-part row: two tall images butted together (each about 535x610px: a hand holding a phone on black, a man in a printed tee) and a 330px sidebar of blog posts, each a bold 14px title, two grey truncated lines and a small-radius thumbnail.
references.type: Aeonik throughout: light 52px for the headline, regular 20 to 24px for mid-page statements, bold 13px for nav chips and post titles, 12px grey captions. Single words switch to an italic serif inside headings. The scale is deliberately small; nothing exceeds 3.6vw.
references.colour: #181818 #070707 #2a2a2a #ffffff #ff4a2b #8a8a8a — Charcoal ground with black chips and white text, unchanged from section to section; colour arrives only through work thumbnails in orange-red, purple and green. A light-mode toggle exists.
references.imagery: Client work as photographs, UI shots, brand graphics and generated explorations; rectangles with 4px corners in tight 4:3 strips and a masonry of mixed aspect ratios, each with a tiny caption.
references.layout: 8px margins and 4 to 8px gutters everywhere. Short three-line statements at about 22px are indented to the 33% or 66% column and act as section breaks between tightly tiled image grids. Text columns stay narrow; images take two-thirds of the width.

sections.description: Rows divided by hairlines, each about 120px tall. The left third holds a small client icon, the name in 12px bold and the sector in grey at the top, with a two-line 11px description pinned to the bottom of the row. The right two-thirds holds three equal 4:3 thumbnails with 4px gaps. Above the list a three-line statement at 22px sits at the 66% column with a text link far right.

A statement at the 66% column introduces a dense masonry of experiments: around twenty tiles in six uneven columns with 4px gaps, sizes from 90px squares to a 280x160px feature tile, mixing screenshots, posters, renders and textures. Every tile has a 10px caption beneath in the form 'Name / Type'. No hover chrome is visible; it reads like a contact sheet.

Two wide video stills side by side, each cropped to a shallow band about 95px tall, showing a person mid-interview. Under each: a black square play chip, a small company icon, then the name in bold 12px and the role in grey. There is no quotation text at all; the testimonial is the video.

Four equal columns headed at 20px, each a list of 11px grey links prefixed by a tiny coloured square icon. Below, a large white circle logo with a black rounded square inside at far left, a two-line 20px question at the 33% column, and a small white booking chip with email and phone set inline beside it.

steal: Shrink page margins and gutters to 8px and tile media edge to edge so a portfolio reads as a working dashboard rather than a brochure.
Put a live blog or news sidebar inside the hero next to the showreel, so the first screen proves the studio is active.
Style nav links as tiny solid rectangular chips sitting directly in the page corner instead of in a bar.
references.media: A muted, looping reel of brand work covers about 51% of the first screen (75% of the width, 68% of the height) in a black well beside a rail of three 16:9 news thumbnails. Below: third-split rows with a label column on the left and three 3:2 tiles on the right two thirds, half-and-half video testimonials, an 8-column masonry of mixed ratios with small captions, and a text panel beside a photo stack; 34 images and 17 videos, client work supplying all the colour on near-black.
references.motion: There is no preloader and only the reel cuts after 400ms; a single ScrollTrigger scrubs the news rail at 0.8 so it drifts as the hero leaves, with no smooth-scroll library and no pins. Cards grow an outline over 0.5s on an ease-out-quint, images move over 0.6-0.8s on cubic-bezier(.19,1,.22,1), links fade colour over 0.2s, and 33 skeleton shimmers (1.2s) hold space while media loads, with no reduced-motion rule.

references.name: The state of the gallery
references.idea: A year-in-review told as a flight over a glowing particle landscape, where each statistic or pick is a single word floating in 3D space.
references.hero: The desktop capture caught the loader: a blue-black screen with a faint dot grid, a 4px acid-yellow progress bar across the top edge, the small logo centred at the top, and a percentage counter at 13.9vw (200px) in thin pale blue-grey grotesk anchored bottom-left. The loaded hero, seen on mobile, splits the title in two: the first two words top-left and the last three bottom-right at the same giant size, with a centred uppercase paragraph between them, all over a full-bleed terrain of olive-green haze and yellow particles. Tiny capital labels occupy all four corners.
references.type: Overused Grotesk only, regular weight: display words at 5 to 14vw in pale blue-grey with a faint lilac sheen, small parenthesised counts set as superscripts beside them, and 10px uppercase captions and corner labels. Two sizes and no bold.
references.colour: #08090d #515721 #b9c6cd #e6f21a #c8b9ee — Blue-black ground; the olive-to-acid-yellow glow of the particle field is the single colour. Type is cool pale grey with a lilac tint, and the yellow loader bar is the brightest element.
references.imagery: A procedural landscape of soft olive fog ridges with thousands of yellow-white points streaming toward the horizon in perspective; later, a curved floor of small tilted white tiles standing for catalogued sites. No photographs.
references.layout: One pinned canvas with a text overlay. Four corner labels stay fixed; each scroll step puts a single word or name at the centre with a one-line caption beneath it in the lower third. Nothing else appears on screen.

sections.description: Full-bleed particle terrain. One category word is centred at about 5vw in pale iridescent grotesk, with its count in parentheses set small and raised at the word's top-right like a superscript. A single-line uppercase caption at 10px sits centred roughly 20% below. Behind the word the particles briefly cluster into the shape of a large numeral. Corner labels are unchanged.

A top-pick slide: a tiny uppercase label above, then the pick's name centred at about 5vw and partly occluded by the scene. Below it dozens of small white rectangular tiles lie on a curved, receding floor grid, some flat and some tilting up toward the camera, growing larger toward the bottom edge of the viewport. A one-line caption sits under the name.

steal: Split a title in two and pin the halves to opposite corners, top-left and bottom-right, at the same giant size with the supporting paragraph centred between them.
Attach a count to a big word as a small parenthesised superscript at its top-right instead of building a stat card.
Make the loading percentage the first giant typographic element, anchored bottom-left under a full-width accent progress bar.
references.media: One fixed WebGL canvas is the only surface: a particle landscape covers 99% of the first screen with the title straight on it, and as you travel the particles leave the ground to form numerals, a figure, floating screenshot cards and a tile-grid panel, while streams of thumbnail tiles fly low between beats. No img or video elements.
references.motion: A percentage preloader is still at 89% at 4.5s, though the load event fired at 2.1s; after it the wheel is captured, each step easing the camera forward to the next beat, with text-free fly-through steps between them (5 of 13 screens show only terrain). Characters rise with a stagger, transform and opacity over 0.7s cubic-bezier(0.22,1,0.36,1) on 704 spans, 0.42s for secondary lines, and counts pop in with an overshoot from 0.6 to 1.08 to 1.
